paragraphs: Rabbi Abba bar Acha. (Rav Acha, his son; see there.) Rabbi Ilai said in Rabbi Abba bar Acha’s name, in our master’s name—Rashi explains: Rabbi. He is not Rabbi Abba bar Acha, father of Rabbi Chiyya the great. In chapter Sheloshah She'akhalu, 49, beginning of a: Rabbi Ila said in Rabbi Yaakov’s name, in Rabbi Abba bar Acha’s name, in our master’s name. (I did not find this reading cited by Yuchasin. Our reading there is: Rabbi Ila said in Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha’s name. At 22a: Rabbi Ila said in Rabbi Acha bar Yaakov’s name, in our master’s name—Rashi explains: Rav. At 25, beginning of b: Rabbi Acha bar Abba bar Acha, in our master’s name.) Here too I was uncertain whether he might be Rabbi Abba without qualification. (First chapter of Shekalim: Rabbi Bibi b.A.; but in the Jerusalem Talmud: Rabbi Ba b.A.) Rabbi Abba of Akko (see above, Rabbi Abba). In chapter Makom Shenahagu (I do not know why he cited chapter Makom Shenahagu): he would kiss the rocks of Akko (Ketubbot 112a). In chapter 2 of Ketubbot (22a): Rabbi Zeira said, “I heard this matter from Rabbi Abba; were it not for Rabbi Abba of Akko, I would have forgotten it.” He was very humble (more than Rabbi Abbahu; see there). They were appointing Rabbi Abbahu as head of the academy, but he declined because Rabbi Abba of Akko had many debts; they should appoint him head of the academy so that he would become wealthy through the gifts they would give him. (Such was their practice: to enrich the head of the academy.) Sotah 40a.
